library_preparation_preflight.summary: org.bytedeco:openblas ships native OpenBLAS binaries only in platform-classifier jars, not the plain group:artifact:version jar the scaffold template adds; without the linux-x86_64 classifier on the test runtime classpath, JavaCPP's Loader cannot find libopenblas and any test touching the BLAS/LAPACK API throws UnsatisfiedLinkError in both JVM and native-image runs.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: No environment variables or system properties are required for the default backend: JavaCPP's Loader auto-extracts and loads the bundled native libraries once the linux-x86_64 classifier jar above is on the test runtime classpath. (Only if a test deliberately wants to swap the BLAS backend, e.g. to Intel MKL, would it need -Dorg.bytedeco.openblas.load=<lib> — not needed for normal OpenBLAS usage.)
risks: Chose the single linux-x86_64 classifier over the upstream-recommended org.bytedeco:openblas-platform aggregator to match repo convention and avoid pulling ~120MB of native jars for platforms the CI/native-image build never runs on; this assumes tests only need to execute on Linux x86_64, consistent with how other native-classifier libraries in this repo are set up.

Local Gradle and native-image verification remain authoritative — if generated tests end up needing additional OpenBLAS entry points not covered by the bundled libjniopenblas.so, that would surface as a runtime/link failure during verification, not from this research.
